programme.title: Great British Menu

programme.title: Great British Menu

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: All three chefs are honouring Wimbledon and the British summer with their technically challenging strawberry desserts. Only the two highest scorers will go through to cook for the judges.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: The two remaining chefs compete for a place in the national finals. To get there they'll have to impress the formidable panel of judges: Oliver Peyton, Matthew Fort and for the first time this year, broadcaster and restaurateur Andi Oliver.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: Tom Parker is eager to impress with a salad that includes 10 elements. Meanwhile, Paul Askew, hopes his traditional techniques will triumph over his younger competitors, and Ellis Barrie is taking a risk with a creative cucumber and oyster starter.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: It is the fish course and the atmosphere in the kitchen gets even tenser as the three newcomers begin to understand the perfection and skill the veteran chef demands. Ellis Barrie attempts to create the flavour of a summer barbecue.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: It is the main course and the pressure is intense in the kitchen. In the hope of impressing the veteran judge, Paul Askew is serving an extremely personal main course based on his mother's favourite food.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: Dessert is the last chance for the chefs to secure a place cooking for the judges and the pressure in the kitchen is intense. Paul can't afford to make any mistakes and is pushing himself with a technically challenging baked alaska.

programme.title: Great British Menu

programme.title: Great British Menu

programme.desc: On tiny islands in the tropical Pacific, Komodo dragons fight for leftovers and fiddler crabs joust on the beach. Under the waves, manta rays and walking sharks patrol the deep.

programme.title: Arabian Seas
programme.desc: The seas of Arabia are alive with carnivores. Sharks and rays patrol the coral reefs hunting down their prey.

programme.title: Strange Creatures
programme.desc: The peacock mantis, when threatened by predators, unfurls its wings, showing warning colours and patterns.

programme.title: Strange Creatures
programme.desc: Exploring interesting types of camouflage and colouration in animals.

programme.title: City Wildlife Rescue
programme.desc: The rescue team is working around the clock to keep up with a baby cedar's feeding demands. Wax wings are filling the aviaries.

programme.title: City Wildlife Rescue
programme.desc: Local residents report seeing a young red tailed hawk walking around their property. The team has to capture him to find out why he's not in the sky. The rescue team also responds to a call about an opossum stuck in a fence.

programme.title: Kenya Wildlife Diaries
programme.desc: Grévy's zebras population has dropped by 50 in less than 20 years. Environmentalists say that if we aren't vigilant, they could disappear all together.

programme.title: Zambia Untamed
programme.desc: As temperatures soar, lagoons and waterholes are drying up. This forces Mvula and his family to undertake a long and dangerous journey to the only remaining source of water, the Luangwa River.

programme.title: Over Australia
programme.desc: Created by titanic forces, the Great Dividing Range separates a thin ribbon of green from the continent's arid heart.

programme.title: Pridelands: Wilderness Reborn
programme.desc: An Australian family go on an adventure to restore an old hunting ranch in South Africa. Their goal is to rebuild the overgrown habitat, create an eco-tourism ranch, and allow the natural wildlife, including predators, to move back in.

programme.title: Arctic Secrets
programme.desc: This episode visually illustrates how the Arctic, locked in darkness for nearly seven months, springs to life once the sun rises above the horizon. We explore ideas of migration, hibernation, the food web and habitat change.

programme.title: Arctic Secrets
programme.desc: Devon Island is the largest uninhabited island in the world, so remote and forbidding that scientists chose Devon to simulate living conditions on Mars. Devon's barren landscape only supports the hardiest of plants and animals.

programme.title: Land of Gremlins
programme.desc: A family of lemurs in the rainforest of Mantadia National Park.

programme.title: Land of Gremlins
programme.desc: A look at how Madagascar's species have evolved to exploit their various habitats.

programme.title: Land of Gremlins
programme.desc: A look at the cold-blooded residents of Madagascar.

programme.title: Superbeast
programme.desc: Bow down to one of nature's oldest and deadliest apex predators. In a world of chaos and crushing oceanic depths, witness how these ancient hunters successfully adapt, endure and strike their prey with completely unstoppable precision.

programme.title: Chasing the Rains
programme.desc: Anastasia leads her elephant herd north in search of a river, cheetah Kuleta escapes from a pack of hyenas, and wild dog Phoenix has a new baby.

programme.title: Chasing the Rains
programme.desc: The elephants dig wells as the rain suddenly pours; a group of lions kill one of cheetah Kuleta's cubs; wild dog Phoenix fights off a pack of hyena.

programme.title: Chasing the Rains
programme.desc: One of the most majestic, unspoiled and rarely filmed areas in Africa is an exploration of how wildlife including cheetahs, hyenas and elephants survive the cycles of draught and rainfall.

programme.title: David Attenborough's First Life
programme.desc: Sir David Attenborough journeys across the globe to discover how the earliest animals developed on our planet. Attenborough meets expert fossil hunters, and sees on-site some of the most remarkable finds that have transformed our understanding of the first animal life forms, including the first set of eyes and teeth and the first predators and parasites.

programme.title: David Attenborough's First Life
programme.desc: Sir David Attenborough's journey continues in Canada's Rocky Mountains, where fossils document an explosion in animal diversity never seen before or since. Travelling on to North Africa, the rainforests of Australia and the east coast of Scotland, Attenborough discovers how animals evolved to conquer not only the oceans but also the land and air.

programme.title: Deadly Australians
programme.desc: As water flows from Australia's highlands into the seas, an assortment of environmental niches set the stage for multifaceted interactions between predators and their prey.

programme.title: Wolves & Lions: Old Enemies
programme.desc: Across the planet, wolves and lions lead two legendary predator lineages: canids and felines. We explore their differences and similarities, from brute strength to social intelligence, revealing who dominates in each territory.

programme.desc: Exploring the lives of big cats, shining a light on the worlds of leopards, lions, and cheetahs.
